plain_birdwatcher.text: Listen up. That's a skylark. It rises straight up and sings without stopping for several minutes. It sings the whole time it's going up, and the whole time it's coming down. Show-off.
Salisbury Plain is a key bird place: skylarks, stone-curlews, and, since recently, great bustards, huge birds brought back after a century away. They are very heavy and rather embarrassed about it.

plain_shepherd.text: These downs have been grazed for thousands of years. The sheep make the short turf that the wildflowers love. Sheep: the original gardeners.
Don't climb the fence near the red flags. The army aren't interested in sheep, but the sheep aren't interested in the army either. It's a truce.

plain_hillwalker.text: I'm walking the whole chalk spine of England. It starts at Avebury, near here, and runs for 87 miles on tracks older than Rome.
The Wiltshire downs hold more ancient monuments than anywhere in Britain. You can't throw a flint without hitting a barrow. I've stopped trying.

plain_horse_kid.text: From down here the horse looks like a horse. From up there it looks like a bunch of white patches. Nobody knows what to make of that, so we don't mention it.
They have to scrub the horse every few years or it goes green. The county gets very cross if it goes green.
